lines.english: "'A prodigy at the age of ten, talented at fifteen, and a normal person after twenty.' Or so they say, anyway…"
"You're much rougher than you used to be before. It's like you've gone back to being a diamond in the rough."
"Are you suggesting that… I've gone sloppy?"
"If you want to put it like that, then sure… But you're still better than me when I was young. That's something I don't like admitting, even if you're my daughter."
"What's that supposed to mean?"
"I'm saying that you haven't gotten any better, but your potential has increased dramatically."
"What are you trying to say, exactly?"
"Do you happen to know of an old guy by the name Martin Flugel? He's something of a veteran in our field."
"Wasn't he your old teacher…?"
"I've heard he's been saying some nonsense like he won't accept more than two students a year anymore. He's getting on in years, I guess."
"Well, he's over 70 now, isn't he? It's amazing that he's still an active professional in itself."
"He has an audition starting next week. Wanna go?"
"What do you mean, 'go'…? You're not saying…"
"Of course, it will be in Vienna. I don't think that guy could survive a plane ride at his age."
"Since you haven't been overseas recently, I can accompany you to start you off, so what do you say?"
"What do I say?"
"Will you give up after all? I don't mind if you want to play around in Japan for another year."
"That's…"
"Well, think it over. Keep in mind though, the flight is booked for the day after tomorrow, so you've only got a day to spare."
"Wha… That early? Wait, hold on!"
"If you find it difficult to decide now, it might be better to turn it down this time. This will change your whole life, after all."
"Anyway, I'm going to head on home today, so let's talk about this more later. I'll see you…"
"Wait, Mom."
"Hm? What is it?"
"…I get it. I'll go."
